title: Understand Resources for Billing, Budget, and Cost Management

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS gives customers several tools for understanding, predicting, controlling, and allocating cloud costs. The exam wants you to recognize which cost tool to use.
sections.callout: Which cost tool do I use?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
bullets: WHO SPENT IT → Cost allocation tags
GIVE ME THE DETAILS → AWS Cost and Usage Report
sections.callout: ESTIMATE · ANALYZE · ALERT · COMBINE · ALLOCATE · REPORT

sections.title: AWS Budgets
paragraphs: AWS Budgets lets customers define budgets and receive alerts when costs or usage reach configured thresholds. You can establish a budget and monitor actual or forecasted spending against it.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A manager says: Tell me when our AWS spending approaches $5,000 this month.
entries.recognitionCue: Spending threshold, budget limit, cost alert, or usage alert → AWS Budgets

sections.title: AWS Cost Explorer
paragraphs: AWS Cost Explorer helps customers visualize and analyze AWS costs and usage over time. It answers questions about how spending changed, which services cost money, cost trends, and visible usage patterns.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company wants to analyze its AWS spending over the last several months.
entries.recognitionCue: Analyze historical cost, visualize spending, cost trends, or usage trends → AWS Cost Explorer

sections.callout: COST EXPLORER = SHOW ME WHERE THE MONEY WENT

sections.title: Exam Trap — Budgets vs. Cost Explorer

table.caption: Separate warning from investigation
rows: Alert me when cost or usage reaches a threshold
Analyze and visualize cost and usage

sections.title: AWS Pricing Calculator
paragraphs: AWS Pricing Calculator helps estimate the expected cost of an AWS architecture before or while planning deployment.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: An architect is planning a new AWS environment and wants an estimated monthly cost.
entries.recognitionCue: Estimate future AWS costs, model architecture pricing, or make a pre-deployment estimate → AWS Pricing Calculator

sections.callout: PRICING CALCULATOR = WHAT WILL THIS COST?

sections.title: Big Three Cost Tool Comparison

table.caption: Choose by timing and required action
rows: Before: What might this architecture cost?
After or current analysis: Where is our money going?
Watch: Tell me if spending crosses my threshold.

sections.callout: ESTIMATE → CALCULATOR · ANALYZE → EXPLORER · ALERT → BUDGETS

sections.title: AWS Organizations
paragraphs: AWS Organizations helps centrally manage multiple AWS accounts. For billing, one major capability is consolidated billing. Instead of treating every AWS account as a separate billing island, an organization can consolidate billing across member accounts.

sections.title: Consolidated Billing
paragraphs: Consolidated billing provides a combined view of charges across accounts in an AWS Organization.
bullets: Potential sharing of eligible pricing benefits
sections.callout: Combine billing for multiple AWS accounts → AWS Organizations consolidated billing

sections.title: Cost Allocation
paragraphs: A company may have one AWS bill but still need to know which department, application, project, environment, or customer caused each cost. Cost allocation connects parts of the total bill to their owners.
sections.callout: TOTAL BILL → WHO OWNS EACH PART?

sections.title: Cost Allocation Tags
paragraphs: AWS resources can use tags such as Department = IT, Project = GSA, Environment = Production, and Owner = TeamA. Certain tags can be activated for cost allocation.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company wants to separate AWS costs for the marketing and IT departments.
entries.recognitionCue: Department cost, project cost, resource ownership cost, or allocate charges → Cost allocation tags

sections.title: AWS-Generated vs. User-Defined Tags

entries.title: AWS-generated tags
paragraphs: Created by AWS for supported purposes.

entries.title: User-defined tags
paragraphs: Created by the customer to represent organizational information such as CostCenter, Department, Application, or Project.

sections.callout: TAGS HELP ORGANIZE AND ALLOCATE COSTS

sections.title: AWS Cost and Usage Report
paragraphs: The AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) provides detailed AWS cost and usage information. It is useful when organizations need more granular cost reporting and analysis.
sections.callout: Detailed cost data, usage data, billing report, or granular cost information → AWS Cost and Usage Report

sections.title: Exam Trap — Cost Explorer vs. CUR

table.caption: Separate visual exploration from detailed reporting
rows: Visual analysis of cost and usage trends

sections.title: Billing Information
paragraphs: AWS provides billing information through AWS billing and cost-management capabilities. Customers should understand where to find current charges, billing information, cost details, payment-related information, and cost-management tools. The exam usually tests which tool best matches the business requirement rather than asking you to memorize every screen.
sections.callout: Charges, invoices, and billing details → AWS Billing and Cost Management

sections.title: Pricing Information
paragraphs: AWS service prices vary by service, Region, usage, resource configuration, storage class, data transfer, and purchasing model. Check current AWS service pricing dimensions when exact pricing matters.
bullets: Actual usage and cost trends → AWS Cost Explorer
Detailed billing records → AWS Cost and Usage Report
sections.callout: Choose the tool by whether you need an estimate, analysis, alert, or detailed record.

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Alert if monthly AWS spending exceeds $1,000 → AWS Budgets
Examine spending trends over six months → AWS Cost Explorer
Estimate a proposed architecture before deployment → AWS Pricing Calculator
Centralized billing for 20 AWS accounts → AWS Organizations consolidated billing
Separate AWS costs by department → Cost allocation tags
Highly detailed cost and usage reporting → AWS Cost and Usage Report
sections.callout: Turn the business verb into the AWS cost tool.

sections.title: GSA Exam Traps

entries.title: Budgets vs. Calculator
paragraphs: Alert about spending → Budgets. Estimate a future architecture → Pricing Calculator.

entries.title: Calculator vs. Cost Explorer
paragraphs: Estimate before deployment → Pricing Calculator. Analyze actual or historical costs → Cost Explorer.

entries.title: Cost Explorer vs. CUR
paragraphs: Visualize or analyze trends → Cost Explorer. Detailed granular billing report → Cost and Usage Report.

entries.title: Organizations vs. Tags
paragraphs: Combine multiple-account billing → Organizations. Identify which department or project generated cost → Cost allocation tags.
